name: remember-the-ladies-letter
description: Abigail Adams urged her husband to remember women in the new nation's laws, or women would foment a rebellion.

name: declaration-rights-woman-gouges
friendly_name: Declaration of the Rights of Woman
description: A French playwright answered the revolution's declaration of rights by demanding equal civil and political rights for women.

name: vindication-rights-of-woman
friendly_name: Vindication of the Rights of Woman
description: Mary Wollstonecraft published a landmark book arguing that women deserve education and a full place in public life.

name: new-jersey-ends-women-voting
description: A state that had quietly let propertied women vote changed its law to limit the franchise to white men.

name: world-anti-slavery-convention-women-barred
description: Female delegates were refused seats at an anti-slavery gathering, pushing two of them toward organising for women's rights.

name: ain-t-i-a-woman-speech
description: Sojourner Truth, formerly enslaved, challenged a women's rights meeting in Ohio with a famous speech on race and gender.

name: wyoming-women-vote
description: A western territory became the first place in the United States to give women full voting rights.

name: susan-anthony-arrested-voting
description: A leading campaigner cast a ballot in a presidential election and was arrested and put on trial for it.

name: isle-of-man-women-vote
friendly_name: Isle of Man Women Gain the Vote
description: A small island parliament let propertied unmarried women and widows vote, ahead of nearly everywhere else.

name: australia-federal-women-vote
description: A new federal law gave most Australian women the right to vote and stand in national elections.

name: pankhurst-founds-wspu
description: Emmeline Pankhurst launched a Manchester organisation with the motto deeds, not words, to win votes for women.

name: finland-women-vote-stand
description: Finnish women won the vote and the right to stand for parliament, a first in Europe.

name: emily-davison-derby
description: A suffragette ran onto a racecourse in front of the King's horse and died of her injuries days later.

name: equal-franchise-act-uk
description: British women gained the vote on the same terms as men, lowering the age for women to twenty-one.

name: turkey-women-vote
description: Turkish women won full national voting and candidacy rights as part of the republic's sweeping reforms.

name: france-women-vote-ordinance
description: A provisional government's ordinance gave French women the vote, first used in local elections the next year.

name: argentina-women-suffrage-law
description: Eva Peron campaigned for the law that gave Argentine women the vote, and it passed Congress.

name: india-women-vote-constitution
description: A new constitution gave all adult Indian citizens, women included, an equal vote from the start of the republic.

name: egypt-women-vote
description: A new constitution gave Egyptian women the right to vote and run for office in the post-revolution republic.

name: iran-women-vote-referendum
description: A package of reforms put to a referendum brought votes for Iranian women, drawing fierce opposition from clerics.

name: swiss-women-federal-vote
friendly_name: Swiss Men Vote Yes for Women
description: Swiss men approved a referendum giving women the federal vote, long after most of Europe.

name: liechtenstein-women-vote
description: A close referendum of men gave women the vote in the last European country to do so nationally.

name: south-africa-women-vote-1994
description: Women of every race voted in the country's first fully democratic election, which ended white-minority rule.

name: kuwait-women-political-rights
description: Kuwait's parliament passed a law granting women political rights after years of defeated proposals.

name: saudi-king-promises-women-vote
friendly_name: Saudi King Promises Women the Vote
description: The ruler announced that women would be allowed to vote and stand in municipal elections in a few years.

name: saudi-women-vote-and-run
description: Women in Saudi Arabia voted and stood as candidates in local elections for the first time.
